channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Iran military official says renewed war with US 'likely'
item.description: Iran's military official stated a renewed war with the US is likely due to unfulfilled promises. The Iranian official said evidence showed Washington was not committed to any promises, hours after US President Donald Trump said he was "not satisfied" with a new Iranian negotiating proposal.

item.title: US to cut troop levels in Germany by 5,000 amid Trump spat with Merz
item.description: The US will cut 5,000 troops in Germany amid a row over Iran. The decision to reduce the US deployment to Germany comes amid a row between the two allies over Iran.

item.title: U.S. warns shipping firms they could face sanctions over paying Iranian tolls in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The US warned shipping firms they could face sanctions for paying Iranian tolls. The alert posted Friday (May 2, 2026) by the U. S. Office of Foreign Assets Control adds another layer of pressure in the standoff between the U. S.

item.title: Iran military official says renewed war with U.S. ‘likely’
item.description: Iran delivered a draft proposal to Pakistan on April 30, 2026. Iran delivered the draft to mediator Pakistan on Thursday (April 30, 2026) evening, state media reported without detailing its contents.

item.title: UK’s Starmer eyes banning some pro-Palestine protests
item.description: UK PM Keir Starmer wants to ban some pro-Palestine protests with certain phrases. PM Keir Starmer says the phrase 'globalise the Intifada' should be 'completely off limits'. UK’s Starmer eyes banning some pro-Palestine protests.

item.title: Kosovo to hold snap elections in June
item.description: Kosovo will hold snap elections in June due to political deadlock over the presidential election. Prime Minister Albin Kurti formed a government in February. Kosovo will soon hold its third parliamentary election in a year and a half.

item.title: Pakistan's Map Faux Pas In Peace Talks Meeting With Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistan displayed a map at a meeting with Afghanistan in Istanbul. The map was shown at a meeting held in Istanbul earlier this week. Pakistan's Map Faux Pas In Peace Talks Meeting With Afghanistan.

item.title: Iran executes two for spying for Israel
item.description: Iran executed two individuals, Karimpour and Bakarzadeh, for spying on behalf of Israel. They were accused of passing sensitive information to Mossad and collecting details on government and religious figures.

item.title: US warns shipping firms they could face sanctions over paying Iranian tolls in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The US warned shipping firms of potential sanctions for paying Iranian tolls in the Strait of Hormuz. Payments could be made in digital assets or through informal swaps for safe passage through the strategic waterway.

item.title: Iran Lost $4,800,000,000 In Oil Revenue Due To US Blockade: Report
item.description: Iran lost $4.8 billion in oil revenue due to the U. S. blockade. The blockade has significantly impacted Iran's economy. The loss is substantial, according to a report. A US soldier points a heavy-calibre machinegun at a vessel in the waterway near Iran.

item.title: China's development offers a 'security dividend' to a fractured world
item.description: China's economic development is offering a 'security dividend' to a fractured world, according to a recent report. The report highlights China's growing influence in global affairs. China's development offers a 'security dividend' to a fractured world news. cgtn. com.

item.title: Hezbollah's Fibre-optic Drones Pose New Challenge For Israel
item.description: Hezbollah has begun using fibre-optic drones, posing a new challenge for Israel in the region. The drones are characteristic of asymmetrical warfare tactics. Hezbollah's use of these drones is characteristic of asymmetrical warfare.

item.title: Rats and weasels infest camps for displaced Gazans
item.description: Displaced Gazans are struggling with infestations of rats and weasels in their camps, which are spreading diseases. The pests have become a daily challenge for residents in the Gaza Strip.

item.title: Trump Warns Of More Oil Disruptions, US Aircraft Carrier Leaves Gulf
item.description: US President Trump warned of more oil disruptions. A US aircraft carrier has left the Gulf region. US Israel Iran War Ceasefire News LIVE Updates. Trump Warns Of More Oil Disruptions, US Aircraft Carrier Leaves Gulf.

item.title: Trump Approves Nearly $9 Billion Weapons Sales To Israel, UAE, Other Mideast Allies Amid Iran War
item.description: US President Trump approved nearly $9 billion in weapons sales to Israel, the UAE, and other Middle East allies. The sales come amid rising tensions with Iran. Representational Image. Trump Approves Nearly $9 Billion Weapons Sales To Israel, UAE, Other Mideast Allies Amid Iran War.

item.title: Germany's Iran "Humiliating" US Comment Costs It 5,000 American Troops
item.description: The US is withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany over six to twelve months. The Pentagon said the withdrawal was expected to be completed over the next six to twelve months.

item.title: Spirit Airlines shuts down, industry's first Iran war casualty
item.description: Spirit Airlines shut down due to high jet fuel prices during the Iran war. Thousands of jobs were lost. The collapse of Spirit will result in thousands of lost jobs and marks the first airline to fail in part due to a doubling in jet fuel prices during the two-month-old Iran war.

item.title: South Korea’s Cherry Blossoms Attract a Connoisseur: The Japanese
item.description: Japanese tourists are viewing cherry blossoms in South Korea. They also practice hanami in Japan. Cherry blossom viewing, or hanami, is a cherished rite in Japan. Some Japanese are also doing it in South Korea.

item.title: Learning Muay Thai Can Allow Visitors to Stay in Thailand Longer
item.description: Thailand offers a five-year visa to visitors who take Muay Thai lessons. Visitors can apply for a five-year visa if they take lessons in “soft power” activities like the Thai martial art.

item.title: Iran announces ‘new rules’ for Strait of Hormuz as US refuses to lift naval blockade
item.description: Iran has announced new regulations for the Strait of Hormuz, as the US maintains its naval blockade. The development escalates tensions in the region, with Iran responding to US refusal to lift the blockade.
